blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it

findings.recommendation: Flatten `import` and name its rules. The seat-adding loop sits six levels deep (for / if / match / if / for / if / if), and a reader stumbles on three questions the code does not answer without the plan: why seats are added to an existing account only when its plan differs from the row's (`account.plan != row.plan` — it reads like a bug), why a seat without '@' is silently skipped (`seat.contains('@')`), and why rows with an empty email are skipped. Use `continue` for the empty-email row (`if row.email.is_empty() { continue; }`), merge the two nested `if`s into one condition, and extract the seat loop duplicated between the `Some` and `None` arms (lines 19-26 and 31-36) into a helper such as `add_valid_seats(db, account_id, seats, existing) -> Result<usize, DbError>` with a named predicate like `is_valid_seat_email`. Add a short comment giving the why of the plan-mismatch condition and of the '@' filter. No behavior change.
findings.title: `import` nests six levels deep and hides its rules in unexplained conditions
